quarterly_data.signal: Ordering of the optical transition changed inside Marvell in the last six months: Murphy said what has hit them is that NPO, or near package optics, probably will hit first in a bigger way, and then CPO's coming — it is all coming, but not at once, and certain customers are going to adopt CPO. The Celestial AI and Inphi photonics teams are now one organisation under Celestial AI's CEO, who also runs Marvell's silicon photonics, the DCI module business and the entire switching platform. The same silicon-germanium TIA and driver content Marvell has shipped for a decade is required for NPO and for linear-drive CPO, on top of 15 billion hours of silicon photonics reliability data.

contracts.signal: Murphy sized NVIDIA's stake in Marvell and disclosed the IP element of the agreement: NVIDIA did a $2 billion investment into Marvell earlier this year, and part of that agreement was Marvell being able to use NVIDIA's IP in its own custom products so they interoperate with NVIDIA merchant products.
contracts.type: equity investment and IP licensing agreement

quarterly_data.signal: Custom is penetrating faster than Marvell modelled: when the company sized this two years ago it assumed maybe 25% penetration of custom silicon versus merchant, and Murphy now says the prevailing view is that number is probably going to be higher in terms of units, while still rejecting the idea that custom takes the whole market. On XPU-attach he repeated the a-year-ago count of 15 or 18 different designs across all four big hyperscalers plus others, spanning the TPU, Trainium and MTIA ecosystems and also attaching to merchant GPUs, and put the content at up into the $500,000, $2,000 content level per accelerator — chips that are almost entirely Marvell IP, built to spec with little customer RTL.
quarterly_data.figure: custom-vs-merchant penetration assumed at 25% penetration now seen higher in units; 15 or 18 different designs across all four big hyperscalers; $500,000, $2,000 content level per accelerator

quarterly_data.signal: Memory expansion is accelerating on the memory shortage: Marvell's organically developed CXL line (expanders, pooling devices, CXL switches and CXL retimers, plus custom memory-expansion silicon) is on turbocharge, with customers that were already designing Marvell in now trying to go faster because expansion obviates the need to buy as much memory as they thought before, while inference KV caching drives disproportionate memory attached to the XPU. Murphy called it a billion, multi-billion dollar kind of business for us in the future with product and market leadership.
quarterly_data.figure: a billion, multi-billion dollar kind of business for us in the future
